title: Package Registry
concept: The XIOM package registry — publish your packages for others to use, discover community packages, and manage dependencies at scale.
why: A language's ecosystem is its packages. The registry connects package authors with users, enabling code reuse, discovery, and versioned distribution.
theory:
## The XIOM Package Ecosystem

### Registry Architecture

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│       XIOM Package Registry      │
│  registry.xiom-lang.org          │
├──────────────────────────────────┤
│  Package Index (searchable)      │
│  Version History                 │
│  Documentation (auto-generated)  │
│  Dependencies Graph              │
│  Download Statistics             │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Publishing a Package

```sh
# Login to the registry
xiom pkg login

# Publish your package
xiom pkg publish

# Publishing checklist:
# ✓ package.xi has name, version, description
# ✓ All tests pass
# ✓ Documentation is written
# ✓ CHANGELOG is updated
# ✓ License is specified
# ✓ Repository URL is correct
```

### Package Metadata

```xiom
package mylibrary
  version "1.0.0"
  description "A library for processing images"
  author "Team XIOM <team@example.com>"
  license "MIT"
  repository "https://github.com/user/mylibrary"
  keywords ["image", "processing", "graphics"]
  categories ["multimedia", "image-processing"]

  deps [
    { name: "xiom.math", version: "^0.5.0" },
  ]
```

### Discovering Packages

```sh
# Search the registry
xiom pkg search image processing

# View package details
xiom pkg info mylibrary

# Show package versions
xiom pkg versions mylibrary

# View documentation
xiom doc mylibrary
```

### Private Registries

```sh
# Configure private registry
xiom config set registry.url https://packages.mycompany.com
xiom config set registry.token $REGISTRY_TOKEN
```

### Package Lifecycle

```
1. Create → 2. Develop → 3. Test → 4. Document →
5. Publish (v0.1.0) → 6. Iterate → 7. Stabilize (v1.0.0) →
8. Maintain → 9. Deprecate → 10. Archive
```
syntax_ref:
# Publish:
xiom pkg login
xiom pkg publish

# Discover:
xiom pkg search <query>
xiom pkg info <package>

# Use:
xiom pkg install
xiom doc <package>
tips: Fill in all package metadata — description, keywords, categories — for discoverability
Publish early (v0.1.0) and often — get feedback before stabilizing at v1.0
Auto-generated docs from xiom doc are published alongside your package — write good doc comments
A well-maintained package has: passing CI badge, updated docs, responsive issues, recent commits
common_mistakes: Publishing without proper version — v0.1.0 is for experimentation, v1.0.0 for stability
Yanking a version that others depend on — deprecate instead, with a migration path
Not updating docs when publishing a new version — out-of-date docs are worse than no docs
